question_text: A 27-year-old woman seeks an evaluation from her gynecologist complaining of vaginal discharge. She has been sexually active with 3 partners for the past year. Recently, she has been having pain during intercourse. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99.1°F), the blood pressure is 110/80 mm Hg, and the pulse is 78/min. The genital examination is positive for cervical motion tenderness. Even with treatment, which of the following complications is most likely to occur later in this patient's life?
